annotationRationale: Combinations count unordered vertex triples. Integer-coordinate step restrictions identify every possible collinear direction, and counts along those lines remove all degenerate triples.
sourceMethod: Followed the official count-all-triples-and-subtract method. Added a reduced-slope argument proving exhaustiveness and explained the three triples for each slope of magnitude 2 or 1/2.

review.mathCheck: There are \(\binom{25}{3}=2300\) distinct triples. A primitive nonaxis direction supporting three points must satisfy \(p,|q|\le2\), leaving only slopes \(\pm1,\pm2,\pm1/2\). Collinear counts are 50 horizontal, 50 vertical, 20 for each unit slope, and 3 for each remaining slope: 152 total. Therefore 2148 triangles, choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithfully rewords MAA solution 23's combinations-minus-collinear-triples approach. It adds an appropriate justification that the official slope list is exhaustive.
review.annotationCheck: Combinations and lattice restrictions are assessed; the combination formula and slope interpretation are background. Inclusive endpoints, skipped grid points, and avoidance of double subtraction are handled correctly.
